formationLabel: Catholic mission worship documented from 1889 · separate territorial parish established 1933 · merged and reestablished as Saint Mary-Saint Jerome Parish in 2012
currentUse: Regular Roman Catholic worship continues at St. Mary Church, 85 South Madison Street, as a worship site of Saint Mary-Saint Jerome Parish. The current diocesan page does not establish current Lithuanian-language ministry. Lithuanian devotional art remains documented in the church by attributed field history.
summary: St. Mary in Custer developed from Catholic mission worship begun in 1889 into a separate territorial parish in 1933. Contemporary diocesan descriptions cited by Wolkovich show that Lithuanians formed a large share of the parish, but the institution was not a Lithuanian national parish. A 1958 fire destroyed the church then in use, and the later church preserves Lithuanian devotional art. St. Mary merged with St. Jerome of Scottville in 2012 to form Saint Mary-Saint Jerome Parish; Catholic worship continues at 85 South Madison Street, while current Lithuanian ministry is not established.

The Diocese of Grand Rapids identifies the combined parish as reestablished in 2012, and its planning summary directs St. Jerome of Scottville to merge with St. Mary of Custer while maintaining the church.

historicalNarrative.text: Catholic worship in Custer began as a mission rather than a Lithuanian national parish. Wolkovich dates mission attendance under the Ludington pastor to July 14, 1889. The exact host church and address during this phase have not been established.

sources.locator: Wolkovich, Lithuanian Religious Life in America, Vol. 3, printed pp. 82-83

historicalNarrative.text: St. Mary became a separate territorial parish in 1933. Wolkovich reports about 200 families at that point, roughly half Lithuanian. Later diocesan descriptions varied from predominantly American Lithuanian to no stated ethnic composition, confirming that Lithuanian community influence and canonical parish form were separate dimensions.

sources.locator: Wolkovich, Lithuanian Religious Life in America, Vol. 3, printed pp. 82-83, 1933 and later diocesan descriptions

historicalNarrative.text: The church then serving St. Mary burned on February 2, 1958 and was rebuilt. The available account does not identify the destroyed building's street address or establish whether the rebuilding immediately produced the same physical structure now standing at South Madison Street.

sources.locator: Wolkovich, Lithuanian Religious Life in America, Vol. 3, printed p. 83

historicalNarrative.text: Lithuanian heritage remained visible in the later church even though St. Mary was territorial. Field documentation attributes the late-1960s church design to Jonas Mulokas and identifies an Our Lady of Vilnius relief with a Lithuanian inscription and a statue of Our Lady of Šiluva. The same account explicitly states that the region's Lithuanian settlers generally attended and influenced local Catholic churches instead of erecting canonical ethnic parishes.

sources.locator: Custer and New Lithuania sections, attributed field history and identity boundary

historicalNarrative.text: In 2012 St. Mary and St. Jerome of Scottville were merged, creating the reestablished Saint Mary-Saint Jerome Parish. The Diocese of Grand Rapids continues to list St. Mary Church at 85 South Madison Street with regular Masses. This is continuing site and successor-parish life, not uninterrupted survival of St. Mary as the former separate institution, and the current sources do not establish Lithuanian-language worship.

conflictsWithArchiveRecord: The 1889 date belongs to mission worship, while 1933 is the formation of a separate territorial parish. Descriptions of Lithuanian predominance document community composition and heritage, not canonical national-parish status. The 1958 fire and rebuilding are established, but the available evidence does not fully reconcile that sequence with the secondary late-1960s date attributed to the present church.
gaps: The exact mission host and address; the address and footprint of the pre-1958 church; the complete post-fire building sequence and dedication dates; the merger instrument and exact effective date within 2012; sacramental-record custody; any parish cemetery; and evidence of current Lithuanian-language ministry remain unresolved.
